segments.chapter: Leading the Basie band: music, rivals and recordings
segments.title: The Stockholm pianist who knew no tunes
segments.summary: He tells of the Swedish bandleader-pianist who didn't know standards.

segments.chapter: Leading the Basie band: music, rivals and recordings
segments.title: End of the first day; second day opens
segments.summary: The first session ends and Berger opens day two with a question about arrangers.

segments.chapter: Leading the Basie band: music, rivals and recordings
segments.title: Arrangers for the Basie band and nights at the Famous Door
segments.summary: Dameron, Harding, Durham and Mundy wrote for the band, and the Famous Door drew stars like Ray Noble.

segments.chapter: Leading the Basie band: music, rivals and recordings
segments.title: Ellington plays 'Prelude to a Kiss' at the Famous Door
segments.summary: Ellington sat in with the Basie rhythm section and played the newly written tune.

segments.chapter: Leading the Basie band: music, rivals and recordings
segments.title: Recording with Duke Ellington and the W.C. Handy album
segments.summary: Norman Granz paired him with Ellington and Johnny Hodges; Hank Jones was on standby.

segments.chapter: Leading the Basie band: music, rivals and recordings
segments.title: Recording with Art Tatum, Nat King Cole and Sinatra
segments.summary: He plays with Tatum, recalls an early Nat Cole date at Glen Wallichs' studio and links his success to Basie.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Basie disbands the big band in 1950
segments.summary: Declining crowds forced Basie to break up the band after a Southern tour.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Basie's small group and its reception
segments.summary: Basie formed a small group, kept only Clark Terry, and drew static from audiences.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Why Basie cut his men loose
segments.summary: Edison believes Basie meant to free the veterans to lead their own groups.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Freelancing in Harlem and the Coleman Hawkins Cleveland trip
segments.summary: With no plans, he enjoyed Harlem and bargained over pay with Hawkins on a trip to Cleveland.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: The Four Brothers at the Apollo and Buddy Rich's quintet
segments.summary: He freelanced around New York and worked with Buddy Rich's group.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Norman Granz's first-class treatment and anti-discrimination stance
segments.summary: Granz paid well, flew them first class and canceled if a hall discriminated.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: 'From Spirituals to Swing' and the move from dance halls to concerts
segments.summary: The first concert hall performance was at Carnegie Hall; he reflects on why dance halls faded.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Big band versus small group and traveling alone
segments.summary: He loves the big band sound but has traveled mostly alone, including years with Eddie Davis.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: The Edison-Wess big band in Japan; LA big bands today
segments.summary: The one-off Japan tour had many ex-Basie men; he also describes how tired he gets and how little he practices.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Jazz at the Philharmonic and out-playing Roy Eldridge
segments.summary: He loved the JATP format and tells of waking Eldridge late in San Francisco and beating him that night.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Leading his own New York group, booked by Basie's office
segments.summary: He led a swinging quintet for about six years with Basie's office as manager.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Roland Hanna asks for a draw

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Josephine Baker, moving to California and the Hollywood Palace staff job
segments.summary: He toured with Baker, settled in LA after tax trouble and joined the ABC staff band.

segments.chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
segments.title: Nelson Riddle and Frank Sinatra's 'In the Wee Small Hours'
segments.summary: Edison describes working with Riddle and Sinatra, who he says learned breathing from Tommy Dorsey.

segments.chapter: Style, originality and the younger generation

segments.chapter: Style, originality and the younger generation
segments.title: No resentment of young players being signed

segments.summary: He recalls Russell Smith, Wendell Culley and Joe Wilder, who were denied orchestra jobs because of color.

segments.title: No resentment in the studios
segments.summary: He says he met no hostility from white studio players.

segments.title: Hardest dates: Motown, Riddle, Costa, Billy May and Benny Carter

segments.title: Accompanying vocalists; Billie Holiday as a favorite
